ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within $\triangle ABC$, we have $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=36^\circ$. Point $D$ is located on $AC$, and $BD=BC$. What is the measure of $\angle BDC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=36^\circ$,

it follows that $ \angle ABC=\angle ACB=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ−\angle A)=72^\circ$.

Since $BD=BC$,

it follows that $\angle BDC=\angle ACB=\boxed{72^\circ}$.

From the text, AB=AC, ∠A=36°, and BD=BC. Let x=∠BDC. Since BD=BC, triangle BDC is isosceles, so ∠BCD=x. Because D lies on AC, the angle at C in triangle BDC is the same as the angle at C in triangle ABC: ∠BCD=∠BCA.
